meta.title: Find a venture to join as a partner | 1lev1
meta.description: Looking for a venture to join? Contribute your skills and your time and take a share of the profit in proportion to what you actually gave - without putting in money and without building a business alone.

hero.eyebrow: ◈ Looking for a venture to join? ◈
hero.h1: Join a venture as a partner, not as an employee
hero.sub: You have a craft and some spare time, and you do not have an idea or the capital to start something alone. Joining a rikma gives you a share of the profit in proportion to what you actually contributed - instead of a wage that runs out at the end of the month.

deal.title: What you put in and what you get back
deal.give_d: What you know how to do, and the hours you have. No money required, and no full-time commitment - a few hours a week count too.
deal.get_d: A share of the rikma that grows with every contribution approved for you, and a portion of the profit at that share. It is not a bonus and not a promise - it is ownership recorded while you work.
deal.note: Your share follows actual contribution, so it is not settled by negotiation on day one and does not depend on how well you bargained.

how.title: How it actually happens
how.s1: Find an open mission or resource that fits you - or tell us what you are good at and we will look.
how.s2: Put yourself forward. The rikma's partners approve, or propose different terms - there is no one-sided refusal.
how.s3: Log hours and resources as you work. Each entry is approved by the partners at the moment it happens.
how.s4: When money comes in, the split is already calculated from what each person gave. No argument and no eyeballing.

open.title: What is open right now
open.sub: All of these can be browsed before you sign up:
open.matchCta: Tell us what you are good at

match.title: Tell us what you are good at
match.sub: There is no open mission that fits you right now - so rather than send you to an empty list, we will make the match by hand. A short conversation, and we look for a rikma for you or help open one.

doubts.title: What stops people from joining
doubts.q1_q: How many hours do I have to commit to?
doubts.q1_a: As many as you want. The system counts hours, not attendance - someone who gave three hours gets the share of three hours. You can start small alongside your existing work and scale up if it works.
doubts.q2_q: What happens if I leave partway through?
doubts.q2_a: What you already contributed stays recorded and stays yours - the share you accrued is not erased when you stop. It does dilute over time, because whoever keeps contributing grows the denominator, but it does not go to zero.
doubts.q3_a: No, and that is the difference from the work you know. There is no fixed salary - there is a share of the profit if and when the rikma earns. Which is why this fits as an addition alongside an existing income, not as an immediate replacement for one.
